# Fixtures

## Layout

- `samples/<engine>/<name>` - real save files the user has permitted for testing. Locked to agents and
  never written by tests.
- `synthetic/<engine>/<name>` - generated examples (plain text, LF line endings).
- `expected/<samples|synthetic>/<relative path>.toml` - golden expectations, one per fixture file.

All of `fixtures/**` is treated as binary by `.gitattributes` (no line-ending conversion).

## Expectation format

```toml
# generated by SAVEPRISM_BLESS=1, review before committing
recipe = "compression.lz-string > format.json"
guard = "exact"
```

`recipe` is the detected step kinds joined by ` > `; `guard` is `exact`, `semantic` or `different`.

## Adding an example

1. Put the file under `samples/<engine>/` or `synthetic/<engine>/`.
2. Run `SAVEPRISM_BLESS=1 cargo test -p saveprism-codecs --test golden` to write the expectation.
3. Review the new `.toml` files (is the recipe what you expect? is the guard verdict plausible?).
4. Run `cargo test -p saveprism-codecs --test golden` without the variable; it must pass.
5. Commit the fixture and its expectation together.

A fixture without an expectation, or with a differing one, fails the test and prints the file path,
the expected value and the found value.

## Provenance of synthetic files

| Folder | Made with | How |
|---|---|---|
| `synthetic/json/` | hand-written | Plain JSON in common serializer styles. `tabs.json` mixes tab indentation with a one-line inner array on purpose; its expected verdict is `semantic`. |
| `synthetic/rpgmaker-mv/` | [lz-string](https://github.com/pieroxy/lz-string) 1.5.0 (MIT), Node.js | `LZString.compressToBase64(JSON.stringify(data))`, the call RPG Maker MV uses for `.rpgsave` files. Data is invented (no real player data). Each file was checked with the library's own `decompressFromBase64` before writing (2026-10-22). These files come from the original JavaScript library, not from our code, so they are an independent check of the LZ-String layer. |
| `synthetic/rpgmaker-mz/` | Python 3.11 `zlib`, [`tools/make_mz.py`](tools/make_mz.py) | What RPG Maker MZ does for `.rmmzsave`: `pako.deflate(JSON.stringify(data), {to: "string", level: 1})`, then NW.js writes that one-char-per-byte string as UTF-8. pako is a port of zlib, so Python's zlib at level 1 stands in for it. Data is invented (2026-10-22). Our zlib encoder (miniz_oxide) may not repeat zlib's bytes exactly, so the expected verdict can be `semantic`. |
| `synthetic/rpgmaker-vxace/` | Python 3.11, [`tools/marshal/make_marshal.py`](tools/marshal/make_marshal.py) | Ruby Marshal 4.8 bytes written by our own small writer from the public format description (`doc/language/marshal.rdoc` in the Ruby repository); Ruby itself was not used. What RPG Maker VX Ace (RGSS3, Ruby 1.9) writes: `Marshal.dump(header)` then `Marshal.dump(contents)`. The header is `{:characters, :playtime_s}`; the contents hash holds `Game_System`, `Game_Screen` (Tone/Color `_dump` data), `Game_Variables` (Fixnums, Bignums, floats), `Game_Switches` (true/false/nil), `Game_SelfSwitches` (array keys), `Game_Actors`, `Game_Party` (`@gold`, `@items {1=>5}`), `Game_Map` (an `RPG::Map` with a `Table`), `Game_Player` (a link to an actor's string). UTF-8 strings carry `:E => true`, symbols and objects seen before are written as links, floats use Ruby 1.9's text. `Save02` adds script data with the rarer types (Struct, `marshal_dump`, extended, user class, Regexp, class/module references, hashes with a default, a Shift_JIS string, a US-ASCII string, a binary string, UTF-8 symbols, a cyclic array, linked Float and Bignum). `Save03` has stat bonuses (`@param_plus`), experience of two classes and a script object in `Game_System` that holds an actor, so that actor's slot in `Game_Actors` is an object link. `Data/` is a small game database (`Items`, `Weapons`, `Armors`: arrays of `RPG::Item`/`RPG::Weapon`/`RPG::Armor` with `@id` and `@name`; `System`: an `RPG::System` with the switch and variable names) for the names of the saves. Data is invented (2026-10-23, `Save03` and `Data/` 2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/rpgmaker-xp/` | Python 3.11, [`tools/marshal/make_marshal.py`](tools/marshal/make_marshal.py) | What RPG Maker XP (RGSS1, Ruby 1.8) writes: one `Marshal.dump` per game object (characters, frame count, `$game_system` ... `$game_player`), strings without encodings, floats as `%.16g` text. `Data/` is a small game database as for VX Ace. Data is invented (2026-10-23, `Data/` 2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/rpgmaker-vx/` | Python 3.11, [`tools/marshal/make_marshal.py`](tools/marshal/make_marshal.py) | What RPG Maker VX (RGSS2, Ruby 1.8) writes: one `Marshal.dump` per game object (characters, frame count, last BGM and BGS, `$game_system`, `$game_message` ... `$game_player`), strings without encodings. The party keeps actor ids; the actors have the VX stat bonuses (`@maxhp_plus` ... `@agi_plus`), a battle action that links back to its actor, and one name in Latin-1 (not UTF-8). `Data/` is a small game database as for VX Ace. Data is invented (2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/nrbf/` | Python 3.11, [`tools/nrbf/make_nrbf.py`](tools/nrbf/make_nrbf.py) | .NET BinaryFormatter (MS-NRBF) streams written by our own small writer from the public specification ([MS-NRBF]: .NET Remoting: Binary Format Data Structure); the .NET runtime was not used. `player.sav` is a Unity-like `PlayerData` in `Assembly-CSharp` with an `Int32`, a `Single`, a `Boolean`, a `String`, an `int[]` (`ArraySinglePrimitive`), a `List<string>`, a `Dictionary<string,int>` with `KeyValuePair` objects, a nested class, a single-use and a shared string, and three nulls covered by one `ObjectNullMultiple256`. `player.sav.gz` wraps the same stream with Python `gzip` (`mtime=0`), so the expectation can be `semantic` at the layer. `system-class.nrbf` uses only `SystemClassWithMembersAndTypes`; `class-with-id.nrbf` reuses class metadata with `ClassWithId` and carries `MemberPrimitiveTyped` values; `jagged.nrbf` is a jagged `BinaryArray` of `int[]`; `forward.nrbf` references an object defined later; `rags.rsv` is a RAGS-like save with invented classes. Data is invented (2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/sugarcube/` | hand-written JSON in [`tools/sugarcube/`](tools/sugarcube/), `saveprism-cli encode` | SugarCube 2 save objects (`{title, date, id, state: {index, delta}}`), compact JSON as `JSON.stringify` writes it. `one-moment` has one moment. `multi-moment` has five moments whose deltas follow SugarCube 2's `Diff.diff` encoding (`[2, value]` copy, `0` delete, a nested object difference, `{"~": [1, from, to]}` array splice, a `(revive:map)` Map replaced by a copy) and `state.index` 3, so the last moment comes after the one the game resumes at. Made with `cargo run -q -p saveprism-cli -- encode fixtures/tools/sugarcube/<name>.json --recipe fixtures/tools/sugarcube/recipe.toml -o fixtures/synthetic/sugarcube/<name>.save --backup-dir <scratch folder>` (LZ-String base64, what `LZString.compressToBase64(JSON.stringify(save))` gives). Our own LZ-String encoder made them, so they test the story view, not the LZ-String layer (the MV files do that). Data is invented (2026-10-23). |
| `synthetic/sol/` | Python 3 standard library, [`tools/sol/make_sol.py`](tools/sol/make_sol.py) | Adobe LSO header and AMF0 / AMF3 values described by the public Adobe AMF specifications. The AMF0 example includes scalars, nested objects, ECMA and strict arrays, an object reference, date and typed object. The AMF3 example includes signed 29-bit boundaries, doubles, string and trait references, sealed and dynamic objects, associative and dense arrays, ByteArray and an integer vector. Invented data (2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/gen3/` | [`tools/gen3/make_gen3.py`](tools/gen3/make_gen3.py), Python 3 standard library | Invented Ruby/Sapphire-like, Emerald-like and FireRed-like 128 KiB saves, two save blocks with different indices, six party records covering different substructure orders, and a 16-byte synthetic RTC footer. Python was unavailable in the fixture-generation environment, so the committed bytes were produced by a temporary Node.js reproduction of this generator. All values and bytes follow the public Gen 3 save and Pokémon structure descriptions; no game data is included. |
| `synthetic/javaser/` | OpenJDK 25 throwaway writer under `target/javaser/`; reproducible with [`tools/javaser/make_javaser.py`](tools/javaser/make_javaser.py) | Invented `com.example.game.SaveData` hierarchy with primitive fields, arrays, collections, boxed values, enum, shared strings and custom `writeObject` data; a second stream covers `TC_RESET` and a long string. No game classes or real saves are used. The committed bytes came from the JDK writer; the Python generator reproduces them byte-for-byte (checked 2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/rpgmaker-2k/`, `synthetic/rpgmaker-2k3/` | Python 3.11 standard library, [`tools/lcf/make_lcf.py`](tools/lcf/make_lcf.py) | RPG Maker 2000 / 2003 LCF files written from the public format notes (liblcf): BER numbers, id/length chunks, structs ended by a 0 byte, arrays of structs with element ids, little-endian vectors. `Save01.lsd` (`LcfSaveData`): title, system (switches, variables with negatives and values above 2^24, music and sound structs, 1-byte transitions, booleans), screen and picture structs kept as unknown chunks, actors (one using its database name `"\x01"`, one Windows-1252 name), inventory, targets. The 2000 save stores gold; the 2003 save leaves it out (gold 0) and has the 2003-only fields (`atb_mode`, battle commands, row, ...). `RPG_RT.ldb` (`LcfDataBase`) holds actor, item (with types: item, weapon, shield, helmet), switch and variable names; the 2003 database adds 2003-only chunks and ends with a top-level end mark. Data is invented (2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/renpy/` | Python 3 standard library, [`tools/renpy/make_renpy.py`](tools/renpy/make_renpy.py) | What Ren'Py writes, from the public format of its saves: a zip (`ZIP_DEFLATED`) with `screenshot.png`, `extra_info`, `json`, `renpy_version`, `log` and, for 8.1 and later, `signatures`; `log` is the pickle of `(roots, log)`. The game classes are small stand-ins with Ren'Py's module and class names (`renpy.revertable.RevertableDict`/`List`/`Set`, `renpy.rollback.RollbackLog`, `store.Inventory`), so `pickle` writes the class references a game would; no Ren'Py code is used. `renpy8-0` is protocol 2 (Ren'Py 8.0) with ints of every width, a 2**70 and a 3**200 integer, unicode text, a float in a `RevertableDict`, a `RevertableList`, a `RevertableSet`, a tuple, a game object with an attribute dict, one string stored under three names and one object under two (memo), a namespaced variable and Ren'Py internals. `renpy8-1-signed` is the same with a non-empty `signatures` entry (invented text, not a real signature). `renpy8-3` is protocol 5 (frames, `MEMOIZE`, `STACK_GLOBAL`) with a 3000 item list (more than one frame), bytes and a set. `renpy7` is what Python 2.7's cPickle writes with protocol 2 (Ren'Py 7), made by a small writer in the tool: byte strings (`SHORT_BINSTRING`), `renpy.python.Revertable*` names, a 64-bit int as an `INT` line, a `long`, an old-style object (`OBJ`); the tool loads it back with Python 3's `pickle` to check it. `persistent` is a zlib (level 3) pickle of a `renpy.persistent.Persistent` object; `persistent-signed` has an invented signature line after the zlib stream, as Ren'Py 8.1 appends one. Our zlib encoder does not repeat zlib's level 3 bytes, so the persistent files are `semantic`. Data is invented (2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/tyrano/` | Python 3, [`tools/tyrano/make_tyrano.py`](tools/tyrano/make_tyrano.py) | TyranoScript desktop saves: compact JSON passed through JavaScript `escape()` (ASCII punctuation and spaces as `%XX`, characters above U+00FF as `%uXXXX`), plus the same data through `encodeURIComponent()` (UTF-8 bytes as `%XX`). The data file has three slots under `data[i].stat.f` with numbers, Japanese strings with spaces, booleans and nested objects; the sf file holds system variables. Both encodings are implemented in the generator from the JavaScript specifications. Data is invented (2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/reg/` | Python 3 standard library, [`tools/reg/make_reg.py`](tools/reg/make_reg.py) | Windows Registry exports written from the public `.reg` format. `unity-playerprefs.reg` is a UTF-16LE BOM, CRLF Unity `PlayerPrefs` export (dwords including a negative int, a `hex(b)` double, UTF-8 + NUL strings with non-ASCII text, a long string wrapped over several lines, and a nested subkey). `regedit4-ansi.reg` is a `REGEDIT4` Windows-1252 file. `mixed-types.reg` has `REG_SZ`, `REG_EXPAND_SZ`, `REG_MULTI_SZ`, a binary value and a deletion line. Data is invented (2026-10-24). |
| `synthetic/godot/` | Python 3 standard library, [`tools/godot/make_godot.py`](tools/godot/make_godot.py) | Invented ConfigFile text plus Godot 3/4 Binary Variant values from the public serialization tables. `.encrypted-header.gdec` contains only the documented `GDEC` marker and is skipped by the golden corpus because opening it intentionally returns the encrypted-save error. |

## Personal data

Before adding a real save, remove personal data: user names (also inside paths and file names), Steam IDs,
account or e-mail strings. Prefer a synthetic example when the format can be reproduced without a real save.
